Base Building Compliance Standards
Issued April 2024
Document owned and updated by:
Rob Gisby (EWARTGXR)
Benito Sanchez Sanchez de Puerta (BPPUERTA)
Leonardo Vitale (LEOVITAL)
Lara Leal Pino (LALEAL)
Important Compliance Standards information:
It`s the BBM vendor`s obligation to identify compliance gaps in all Compliance Standards to allocate
maintenance & compliance costs correctly and to keep the serviced site safe.
The Compliance Standards are just a guide and not an exhaustive list of regulatory requirements.

AMAZON BASE BUILDING COMPLIANCE STANDARD
Task Title Enclosed Space
APM Object CT.AIR.ENCSPACE
APM Description Cark parks, workshops and other enclosed spaces.
Follow safety procedures - e.g. 1MRA, LOTO, PPE, etc.
Ensure that all WOs are carried out by qualified, certified staff with appropriate familiarisation and supervision as required
Add notes for each observation and create a FWO if necessary to eliminate defects
General tasks Use appropriate tools, chemicals and industry standard practices (RME policy permitting)
always required Ensure relevant logs, readings and certification is uploaded to APM prior to WO closure. CT evidence must be additionally uploaded to the DMS (WorkDocs in DE)

Scope
All sites where ventilation systems are used as mechanical means of ventilation for enclosed areas, such as car parks, workshops or basements. Note designated “confined spaces” should be managed via site specific controls and are not covered by this standard.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.
This document is considered released as draft.
For Information contact Authors: R Gisby (ewartgxr), Leonardo Vitale (leovital) and Benito Sanchez Sanchez de Puerta (bppuerta)

Any site with an electrical installation. Inspection of the earthing and electrical discharging systems is mandatory as part of the inspection of the electrical installation as a whole.

However, EU RME simplifies to LV < 1 kV AC and HV ≥ 1 kV AC.
Any site where an emergency lighting system (including battery) is installed to aid safety in the event of power failure and/or safe evacuation of the site in emergency situations.
Inspection requirements of electrical installations are covered by "Compliance HV inspection and test", "High/Medium Voltage" and "Low Voltage" Standards.
Any site with an electrical installation. CEN and CENELEC standards define incoming electricity at:
Less than 1 kV - low voltage installations
Between 1 kV and 36 kV - medium voltage installation
Any site where diesel power generators are commissioned to produce electricity, generally as a back-up in emergency situations. This includes all diesel generators, whether stationary or mobile.
This Compliance Standard only covers the inspection requirements associated with the electrical components of diesel generators. The maintenance of a UPS is covered in CT.ELEC.UPS.

Scope
Any site with an electrical installation. Inspection of the earthing and electrical discharging systems is mandatory as part of the inspection of the electrical installation as a whole.
More than 36 kV - high voltage
However, EU RME simplifies to LV < 1 kV AC and HV ≥ 1 kV AC.
Any site where an emergency lighting system (including battery) is installed to aid safety in the event of power failure and/or safe evacuation of the site in emergency situations.
Inspection requirements of electrical installations are covered by "Compliance HV inspection and test", "High/Medium Voltage" and "Low Voltage" Standards.
Any site with an electrical installation. CEN and CENELEC standards define incoming electricity at:
Less than 1 kV - low voltage installations
Between 1 kV and 36 kV - medium voltage installation
Any site where diesel power generators are commissioned to produce electricity, generally as a back-up in emergency situations. This includes all diesel generators, whether stationary or mobile.
This Compliance Standard only covers the inspection requirements associated with the electrical components of diesel generators. The maintenance of a UPS is covered in CT.ELEC.UPS.

APM Object CT.FIRE.FAS
APM Description Fire Alarm System (FAS).
Follow safety procedures - e.g. 1MRA, LOTO, PPE, etc.
Ensure that all WOs are carried out by qualified, certified staff with appropriate familiarisation and supervision as required
Add notes for each observation and create a FWO if necessary to eliminate defects

always required Ensure relevant logs, readings and certification is uploaded to APM prior to WO closure. CT evidence must be additionally uploaded to the DMS (WorkDocs in DE)

Scope
All sites are required to have a suitable and sufficient fire detection system. The complexity of the fire detection system will depend on the site-specific fire risk assessment, which is covered under CT.FIRE.FRAMANAGEMENT, and will be based on the size and complexity of the premises, the
type of activities undertaken or materials stored, the presence of vulnerable occupants and the ease of spotting and making everyone aware of a fire.
Small, single-storey or open-plan premises, where no high-risk substances are stored, no high-risk activities are undertaken, no vulnerable occupants can be present and where a fire is easy to spot and a shout of “fire” would be easily heard might be exempt from requiring a Fire Alarm system.
If either of these conditions does not apply to your premises, then a Fire Alarm System is likely to be required.
Inspection and testing of heat and smoke detectors is covered under CT.FIRE.SMOKEDETECT.
Fire drills and evacuation tests are covered under CT.FIRE.EVACUATION

This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,

Scope
Any site with air conditioning systems with an effective rated output of more than 12 kW, when either an individual unit is ≥ 12 kW or multiple individual units of < 12 kW are connected in the same system to give ≥ 12 kW in total.

Scope
Any site with cold water services, such as water supply storage tanks and distribution network, that might lead to a risk of employees contracting legionella disease (or other water borne pathogen).
Legionella risk assessment requirements are covered under CT.WATER.LEGIONELLA. Hot water systems are covered in CT.WATER.HOTSERVICE and cooling towers in CT.WATER.COOLINGTOWERS.
Additional requirements of emergency showers and eyewashes are covered under CT.SAFE.WASH

Scope
All sites are required under Health and Safety regulations to ensure their employees’ health is maintained. As such, employers have the responsibility of ensuring their water supply is wholesome.
Water provided by the city/municipality/water company should not contain lead in excess of statutory levels. Responsibility for supply and distribution outside the facility boundary is not part of the scope of the standard.

Task Title Equipment used to move goods
APM Object CT.WORK.GOODSMOVE
APM Description Equipment used to move goods/objects, including pick carts, rebin trollies and stow carts.
Follow safety procedures - e.g. 1MRA, LOTO, PPE, etc.
Ensure that all WOs are carried out by qualified, certified staff with appropriate familiarisation and supervision as required
Add notes for each observation and create a FWO if necessary to eliminate defects
General tasks Use appropriate tools, chemicals and industry standard practices (RME policy permitting)
always required Ensure relevant logs, readings and certification is uploaded to APM prior to WO closure. CT evidence must be additionally uploaded to the DMS (WorkDocs in DE)

• Additional detail pages (such as this) have been added to aid useability of the document
• Changes to the template of each PM plan have been made including:(See image below) (See imagine on previous page)
1. APM EC has been added to each plan to assist planners to more quickly identify where the PM
package is allocated
2. Geo’s applied has been added to indicate which APM Instance or regions a plan is available
and/or deployed.
3. F-Gas flag has been added to identify systems which may be linked to F-Gas compliance
4. Source OCB has been added as some PM’s may be based on technologies outside of the BBM
OCB
5. Pricing Template Position has been added to each PM to assist vendors to identify quickly
which discipline the PM relates to on the BBM Vendor Pricing Template
6. Schedule With has been added to indicate Object Codes of equipment which might logically
have their maintenance scheduled at the same time due to similar locations or disciplines.
These are cross referenced to promote use of efficient maintenance scheduling. This is a guide
and intended to support planners.
7. Description of System has been included and updated to mirror the BBM Handbook
8. Additional Information was previously under a different heading and has been moved and
renamed.
9. Change Control section has been added to each PM page to show the incremental changes
made to each PM over time.
Using this document
This is a living document and whilst updates are minimised, this document (and each PM within it) should
be considered living. It is important to avoid taking off-line copies unnecessarily and to actively check the
‘Last Update’ date field for version control.
To suggest improvements to these standards, please use the appropriate links below:
For issues relating to content of standards:
Raise SIM here
For APM related issues
River Link and Path below
https://river.amazon.com
APM Help Center -->  Select Region --> Base Building Maintenance (BBM) --> Standard PM's
Definitions & References
APM – Asset Performance Management, Amazons Computerised Maintenance Management System
(CMMS)
APM Instance – APM operates in two ‘Instances’, one [AMER] covering North America and LATAM, the
other [Intl] covering all remaining regions around the world.
CMMS – Computerised Maintenance Management System [See APM]
EC - equipment configuration acts as a profile for equipment, and populates data (Manufacturer, Model,
Revision, Class and Category) linked with it to the equipment created. Standard equipment-specific data is
linked from the configuration such as Documents, parts associated and PM Schedules.
FWO – Follow-up Work Order (corrective activity)
HIE – High Impact Event
HRO – High Risk Operation as defined by WHS
OCB – Object code builder Nesting - Nesting is simply an indication that higher frequency tasks are included (nested) in lower 
frequency tasks. In practice, this would mean, that all tasks that are (example) scheduled monthly, will also 
be undertaken in the annual maintenance avoiding the need for 2 (or more) work orders to be issued 
concurrently. APM (The CMMS) will automatically accommodate this releasing only the work order with the 
higher interval.
No-Go – No-Go Activity as defined by WHS
PM – Preventative Maintenance – (See also SC) Preventative Maintenance may (unlike SC) be intrusive or
require specialised training, tooling, certification or perimetry etc
Most appropriate delivery mechanism will be subject to local review and may require SOP, task risk
assessment, permits or delivery via sub contracted resource as appropriate. Note:- PM does not
automatically indicate that activity cannot be self-delivered. If one or more of the task items within a
maintenance activity is determined to be ‘PM’, the whole maintenance activity will be classified as ‘PM’.
Corrective work identified during a PM must be raised as a Follow-up Work Order (FWO)
SC – System Check (See also PM) - a sub-type of PM are ‘non-intrusive’ checks or activities and will
generally be self-delivered by technicians with appropriate information, instruction, training and
supervision (which may include SOP) but are usually not intended not to require additional specialist
knowledge, certification.
Note - This is guidance only and local implementation should be subject to local review to ensure safety at
all times.
Corrective work identified during a SC must be raised as a Follow-up Work Order (FWO)
SME – Subject Matter Expert
SOP – Standard Operating Procedure
VSOP – Visual Standard Operating Procedure
Acknowledgements
This document brings together practices from industry standards, manufacturer recommendations,
compliance standards, learnings from HIE/COE and SME input.
Thank you to all who contribute to continue to continue to improve and refine these maintenance activities
which play an important part in standardising our approaches across Amazon.

Oil Separator (Waste water containing oil / gasoline)
Oil separators are designed to prevent oil and other hydrocarbons from entering the drainage system. They separate oil from water, and safely retain the oil until it is removed. Oil cannot be treated easily and will therefore cause severe pollution if allowed to
enter mains sewers or drainage fields. Statutory controls enforce strict regulations on the discharge of such pollutants. Oil separators should be used in such applications as petrol stations, industrial yards and garages; or virtually anywhere that a risk of oil
contamination exists. Discharge requirements for oil separators may vary by region.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
DOCK DOOR: Dock doors are a type of loading dock which are usually raised in the air in order to be level with trucks carrying goods.
DOCK RAMP: Dock ramps act as a liaison between the warehouse and trucks, making up for differences in height and filling the gap between truck and building.
DOCK LOCK: The Lock locks trailers onto the loading bay By locking the rear wheel, the docked vehicles will no longer move away from the dock. Also, vehicle “creeping’, caused by momentum incurred during the loading and unloading process is prevented. This
guarantees optimal safety.
DOCK AIR BAG SEAL: Inflatable lining around the entrance of the Dock door which reduces airflow and dust particles entering in the warehouse when trailers are loading/unloading via the Dock door.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
GATE VALVE: Gate valves are used to isolate the specific area of water supply to the network during maintenance, repair works, new installations, as well as to reroute water flow throughout the pipeline.
BUTTERFLY VALVE: Butterfly valves can be used for throttling or regulating flow as well as in the full open and fully closed position. The pressure loss through a butterfly valve is small in comparison with the gate valve.
PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE: A Pressure Reducing Valve (PRV) is an Automatic Control Valve designed to reduce a higher unregulated inlet pressure to a constant, reduced downstream (outlet) pressure regardless of variations in demand and/or upstream (inlet)
water pressure.
FIRE BACKFLOW PREVENETER: Backflow preventers provide a critical interface between a building's fire protection system and the water supply that feeds it. A backflow preventer is a device designed to ensure that water inside a building's fire sprinkler system

Scope
All sites where Local Exhaust Ventilation systems are used as individual mechanical means of ventilation for activities, processes or areas that are likely to produce fumes, smoke, gas or air emissions which may be toxic or harmful if inhaled/exposed, including those mounted to machinery,
mobile units and fixed units.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.

Scope
Any site where an emergency lighting system (including battery) is installed to aid safety in the event of power failure and/or safe evacuation of the site in emergency situations.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.
This document is considered released as draft.

Any site where diesel power generators are commissioned to produce electricity, generally as a back-up in emergency situations. This includes all diesel generators, whether stationary or mobile.

Scope
Any site where diesel power generators are commissioned to produce electricity, generally as a back-up in emergency situations. This includes all diesel generators, whether stationary or mobile.
This Compliance Standard only covers the inspection requirements associated with the electrical components of diesel generators. The maintenance of a UPS is covered in CT.ELEC.UPS.

Scope
Any site with an electrical installation. Inspection of the earthing and electrical discharging systems is mandatory as part of the inspection of the electrical installation as a whole.
More than 36 kV - high voltage
However, EU RME simplifies to LV < 1 kV AC and HV ≥ 1 kV AC.
Any site where an emergency lighting system (including battery) is installed to aid safety in the event of power failure and/or safe evacuation of the site in emergency situations.
Inspection requirements of electrical installations are covered by "Compliance HV inspection and test", "High/Medium Voltage" and "Low Voltage" Standards.
Any site with an electrical installation. CEN and CENELEC standards define incoming electricity at:
Less than 1 kV - low voltage installations
Between 1 kV and 36 kV - medium voltage installation
Any site where diesel power generators are commissioned to produce electricity, generally as a back-up in emergency situations. This includes all diesel generators, whether stationary or mobile.
This Compliance Standard only covers the inspection requirements associated with the electrical components of diesel generators. The maintenance of a UPS is covered in CT.ELEC.UPS.

Scope
All sites are required to have a site-specific fire emergency evacuation plan which should be based on the risks identified as part of the Fire Risk Assessment (covered under "Fire Risk Management (FRA)")
Fire drills or evacuation tests are essential elements of fire safety and aim to provide a comprehensive understanding of the fire evacuation procedures, risks and strategy to all employees.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.
This document is considered released as draft.
For Information contact Authors: R Gisby (ewartgxr), Leonardo Vitale (leovital) and Benito Sanchez Sanchez de Puerta (bppuerta)

Scope
All sites are required to have a suitable and sufficient fire detection system. The complexity of the fire detection system will depend on the site-specific fire risk assessment, which is covered under CT.FIRE.FRAMANAGEMENT, and will be based on the size and complexity of the premises, the
type of activities undertaken or materials stored, the presence of vulnerable occupants and the ease of spotting and making everyone aware of a fire.
Small, single-storey or open-plan premises, where no high-risk substances are stored, no high-risk activities are undertaken, no vulnerable occupants can be present and where a fire is easy to spot and a shout of “fire” would be easily heard might be exempt from requiring a Fire Alarm system.
If either of these conditions does not apply to your premises, then a Fire Alarm System is likely to be required.
Inspection and testing of heat and smoke detectors is covered under CT.FIRE.SMOKEDETECT.
Fire drills and evacuation tests are covered under CT.FIRE.EVACUATION

Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.

Scope
All non-domestic properties are required to complete a suitable and sufficient Fire Risk Assessment (FRA) specific to each site identifying the risks to relevant persons and the fire precautionary measures that need to be implemented in order to comply with relevant regulations, as well as the
emergency procedures to follow in the event of a fire.
FRAs need to be reviewed and updated regularly to reflect the most up-to-date situation of the premises.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.
This document is considered released as draft.

Scope
Any site with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) aimed to prevent falls of employees working at height. This Compliance Standard covers harnesses, fall arrest systems and fall restraint lanyards.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.
This document is considered released as draft.

Any site that uses vacuum lifting equipment to transport heavy loads. If they vacuum lifting machine is permanently attached to a crane or other lifting equipment it should be thoroughly examined as an integral part of such equipment. In any other instance, it is considered to be a lifting
accessory.

Scope
Any site that operates pressure systems and vessels, such as boilers, condensers, heating and air conditioning devices (vapor compressing), etc associated pipework in which a breach may give rise to danger, primary shut off valves and protective devices. Typically, equipment with steam at
any pressure, gases which exert a pressure in excess of 0.5 bar above atmospheric pressure and fluids which may be mixtures of liquids, gases and vapours where the gas or vapour phase may exert a pressure in excess of 0.5 bar above atmospheric pressure.
Inspection requirements for boilers are covered in CT.HVAC.BOILERS.
Note this standard excludes hired plant e.g. mobile compressors as some responsibilities will fall to the provider.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.

Scope
Any site that uses physical or non-physical barriers as means to prevent, control or mitigate undesired events or accidents.
This Standard is for planned preventative maintenance only. It is expected that pre-use checks are undertaken by operator prior to using the equipment and that equipment would not be used where guarding has been removed or damaged.
Note other guarding is covered in CT.SAFE.CONVGUARDING
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.
This document is considered released as draft.

water system maintenance are:
- Descaling of less worn elements by immersion in acid solution (sulfamic acid, acetic acid, etc.) and
subsequent disinfection (not less than 30 minutes, in cold water containing at least 50 mg/L free chlorine).
- Periodically replacement of faucet valve, faucet water filters, shower heads and pipes, as well as any
other discontinuity element. The frequency of replacement is usually a function of water characteristics.
- Microfiltering that allows the removal of Legionella from the water exiting at the point of use, through a
mechanical barrier.

If a BBM Maintenance activity fully meets the compliance requirements below, periodic upload of PM evidence will be required to APM and DMS / Workdays depending on region.

The key to the below document is as follows:
CT - Amazon compliance / statutory task - not otherwise covered by a BBM Standard PM. Evidence to be provided into APM and DMS upon task closure.
CT* - This is a conditional task based or based on findings from previous inspections. If a frequency is not used, a further appropriate frequency needs to be in either the region, or 'ALL'. Local teams must ensure appropriate frequency.
(CT) - Compliance task which is likely met or exceeded by a CT task in [ALL] and therefore achieved by proxy BUT local site must satisfy themselves that requirements are fully met.
PM - Requirement can demonstrated through appropriate maintenance - Refer to relevant PM Standard
(PM) - Maintenance task which is met or exceeded by a PM task in [ALL] and therefore achieved by proxy BUT local site must satisfy themselves that requirements are fully met including regional / manufacturer requirements.
EVID - Periodic upload of evidence to DMS, for non-CT task lines. For example, evidence of PM completion, certification, licence etc.
EVID* - Conditional requirement to upload evidence at the interval provided
N A R - No Additional Requirement

Scope
Any site where cardboard and plastic balers are used to flatten, stack and bind together cardboard boxes and pieces of carboard and plastic so they can be easier to store or dispose of via a recycling or waste facility.
Using this document
This document is intended as a guide and may not be exhaustive. Whilst this document is based extensively on professional guidance and subject to periodic review, individual sites must be diligent to ensure they are aware of,
and comply to, local and changing regulations.
The format of these standards is intended to improve navigation between maintenance and compliance standards and to allow frequent, minor updates to a single living resource. Please avoid offline or printed versions and check version dates and change log.
In the event of becoming aware of errors or omissions in this document, sites must provide detail, including references to relevant source information to their local planner for escalation - SIM Link above.

PM.text:
Nesting - Nesting is simply an indication that higher frequency tasks are included (nested) in lower 
frequency tasks. In practice, this would mean, that all tasks that are (example) scheduled monthly, will also 
be undertaken in the annual maintenance avoiding the need for 2 (or more) work orders to be issued 
concurrently. APM (The CMMS) will automatically accommodate this releasing only the work order with the 
higher interval.
No-Go – No-Go Activity as defined by WHS
PM – Preventative Maintenance – (See also SC) Preventative Maintenance may (unlike SC) be intrusive or
require specialised training, tooling, certification or perimetry etc
Most appropriate delivery mechanism will be subject to local review and may require SOP, task risk
assessment, permits or delivery via sub contracted resource as appropriate. Note:- PM does not
automatically indicate that activity cannot be self-delivered. If one or more of the task items within a
maintenance activity is determined to be ‘PM’, the whole maintenance activity will be classified as ‘PM’.
Corrective work identified during a PM must be raised as a Follow-up Work Order (FWO)
SC – System Check (See also PM) - a sub-type of PM are ‘non-intrusive’ checks or activities and will
generally be self-delivered by technicians with appropriate information, instruction, training and
supervision (which may include SOP) but are usually not intended not to require additional specialist
knowledge, certification.
Note - This is guidance only and local implementation should be subject to local review to ensure safety at
all times.
Corrective work identified during a SC must be raised as a Follow-up Work Order (FWO)
SME – Subject Matter Expert
SOP – Standard Operating Procedure
VSOP – Visual Standard Operating Procedure

This document brings together practices from industry standards, manufacturer recommendations,
compliance standards, learnings from HIE/COE and SME input.
Thank you to all who contribute to continue to continue to improve and refine these maintenance activities
which play an important part in standardising our approaches across Amazon.

require specialised training, tooling, certification or perimetry etc
Most appropriate delivery mechanism will be subject to local review and may require SOP, task risk
assessment, permits or delivery via sub contracted resource as appropriate. Note:- PM does not
automatically indicate that activity cannot be self-delivered. If one or more of the task items within a
maintenance activity is determined to be ‘PM’, the whole maintenance activity will be classified as ‘PM’.
Corrective work identified during a PM must be raised as a Follow-up Work Order (FWO)
SC – System Check (See also PM) - a sub-type of PM are ‘non-intrusive’ checks or activities and will
generally be self-delivered by technicians with appropriate information, instruction, training and
supervision (which may include SOP) but are usually not intended not to require additional specialist
Note - This is guidance only and local implementation should be subject to local review to ensure safety at
Corrective work identified during a SC must be raised as a Follow-up Work Order (FWO)
This document brings together practices from industry standards, manufacturer recommendations,
compliance standards, learnings from HIE/COE and SME input.
Thank you to all who contribute to continue to continue to improve and refine these maintenance activities
which play an important part in standardising our approaches across Amazon.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
Oil Separator (Waste water containing oil / gasoline)
Oil separators are designed to prevent oil and other hydrocarbons from entering the drainage system. They separate oil from water, and safely retain the oil until it is removed. Oil cannot be treated easily and will therefore cause severe pollution if allowed to
enter mains sewers or drainage fields. Statutory controls enforce strict regulations on the discharge of such pollutants. Oil separators should be used in such applications as petrol stations, industrial yards and garages; or virtually anywhere that a risk of oil
contamination exists. Discharge requirements for oil separators may vary by region.
Additional Information
All sites with the above listed Base Building Asset should conduct routine maintenance and inspections according to this standard PM package. The Amazon maintenance standard supports compliance, reduces safety risks,improves asset reliability & efficiency.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
DOCK DOOR: Dock doors are a type of loading dock which are usually raised in the air in order to be level with trucks carrying goods.
DOCK RAMP: Dock ramps act as a liaison between the warehouse and trucks, making up for differences in height and filling the gap between truck and building.
DOCK LOCK: The Lock locks trailers onto the loading bay By locking the rear wheel, the docked vehicles will no longer move away from the dock. Also, vehicle “creeping’, caused by momentum incurred during the loading and unloading process is prevented. This
guarantees optimal safety.
DOCK AIR BAG SEAL: Inflatable lining around the entrance of the Dock door which reduces airflow and dust particles entering in the warehouse when trailers are loading/unloading via the Dock door.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
A busbar is a metallic strip or bar, typically housed inside switchgear, panel boards, and busway enclosures for local high current power distribution. They are also used to connect high voltage equipment at electrical switchyards, and low voltage equipment
in battery banks. They are generally uninsulated, and have sufficient stiffness to be supported in air by insulated pillars. These features allow sufficient cooling of the conductors, and the ability to tap in at various points without creating a new joint.
Additional Information
All sites with the above listed Base Building Asset should conduct routine maintenance and inspections according to this standard PM package. The Amazon maintenance standard supports compliance, reduces safety risks,improves asset reliability & efficiency.
Some maintenances captures several assets within one PM package -> Ensure that corrective/reactive maintenance for assets where proactive maintenance is contained under another asset is created against the original asset.
Note: This standard PM package is specific to all Busbars which are installed in the FC to distribute electrical power to consumers. Busbars which are installed in any electrical panel/cabinets are always captured in the PM of those equipment.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
An aspirating smoke detector (ASD) is a system used in active fire protection, consisting of a central detection unit which draws air through a network of pipes to detect smoke. The sampling chamber is based on a nephelometer that detects the presence of
smoke particles suspended in air by detecting the light scattered by them in the chamber. ASDs can typically detect smoke before it is visible to the naked eye.
Additional Information
Ensure the filters are changed minimum once a year or according to O&M manual if a shorter interval is recommended

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
Dampers as part of the life safety system open or close during an emergency event. Automatic control dampers are typically found on the exterior of the building and open to provide make-up air for smoke exhaust fans. Fire dampers are installed in an air-
distribution system, that is designed to close automatically upon detection of heat to interrupt migratory airflow and to restrict the passage of flame. Combination Fire/Smoke Damper, is a motorized damper located within HVAC ducting that closes both
detection of fire, and is also interfaced with the fire alarm control unit to close upon the detection of smoke.
Additional Information
All sites with the above listed Base Building Asset should conduct routine maintenance and inspections according to this standard PM package. The Amazon maintenance standard supports compliance, reduces safety risks,improves asset reliability & efficiency.

Description of System / Technology (According to BBM Handbook)
GATE VALVE: Gate valves are used to isolate the specific area of water supply to the network during maintenance, repair works, new installations, as well as to reroute water flow throughout the pipeline.
BUTTERFLY VALVE: Butterfly valves can be used for throttling or regulating flow as well as in the full open and fully closed position. The pressure loss through a butterfly valve is small in comparison with the gate valve.
PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE: A Pressure Reducing Valve (PRV) is an Automatic Control Valve designed to reduce a higher unregulated inlet pressure to a constant, reduced downstream (outlet) pressure regardless of variations in demand and/or upstream (inlet)
water pressure.
FIRE BACKFLOW PREVENETER: Backflow preventers provide a critical interface between a building's fire protection system and the water supply that feeds it. A backflow preventer is a device designed to ensure that water inside a building's fire sprinkler system

A sprinkler system employing automatic sprinklers attached to a piping system containing water and connected to
